title: Standing up for the art, not just the money
summary: Sam and Ridley say musicians must stand up for rights and keep the art alive before others claim it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: But see, the thing that you're talking about Sam that it's so hard for some cats and you know I've had different people run different things back every month. They say well everybody don't think the way you do and blah blah b'ah. But I think it comes to a point where a man has got to be a man and stand up for what you feel is right.
That's right man. If you don't stand up for your rights, there's no one that's going to do it for you.
And like I say, what I'm saying all the time, this interest in the art of the music, man it's not all together the money all the time.
You know it's the art of the thing man, the keeping this thing alive man because pretty soon after all of us is gone man, the white man say that music is his.
And that's what they're trying to do right now.
Do you see what I mean?
